page.title: Settings
page.intro: Your own account, your calendar accounts, and integrations.
page.introAdministrator: Your own account, your calendar accounts and integrations, and who can join this installation and its storage.

ownAccount.title: Sign-in and email
ownAccount.intro: How you sign in to Calendar Ghost, and the email it sends you.

password.title: Password
password.body: Changing it signs you out on your other devices.
password.saved: Your password was changed. Your other devices were signed out.

notifications.title: Incident emails
notifications.body: When one of your rules needs attention, Calendar Ghost can also email you. Activity always lists every incident.
notifications.label: Email me about incidents
notifications.unavailable: Your administrator can set up email for this Calendar Ghost. Until then, incidents appear in Activity.
notifications.unavailableAdministrator: To send incident emails, add SMTP settings to .env and restart Calendar Ghost. Until then, incidents appear in Activity.
notifications.on: Calendar Ghost now emails you about incidents.
notifications.off: Calendar Ghost no longer emails you about incidents. They still appear in Activity.

delete.title: Delete your account
delete.body: Deletes your sign-in, rules, and calendar connections. You choose whether the events your rules wrote go too. Your calendar accounts and your own events stay.
delete.confirmBody: This deletes your sign-in, rules, calendar connections, tokens, and Activity, and signs you out. Choose below what happens to the events your rules wrote. Your own events and your calendar accounts stay as they are. Backups taken before now keep your records until they rotate out. This cannot be undone.
delete.confirmBodyLastUser: You are the last person here. This deletes your sign-in, rules, calendar connections, tokens, and Activity, and Calendar Ghost returns to setup, where the next person to open it creates the administrator. Choose below what happens to the events your rules wrote. Your own events and your calendar accounts stay as they are. Backups taken before now keep your records until they rotate out. This cannot be undone.
delete.needsAdministrator: Someone else must be an administrator before you can delete your account. Make another person an administrator on the People page, then come back.
delete.deleteEventsHint: They are removed from your calendars wherever Calendar Ghost can still reach them.
delete.keepEventsHint: They stay in your calendars, and Calendar Ghost no longer manages them.

registration.title: Who can join
registration.intro: Everyone keeps their own calendars, rules, and Activity private. This decides only who can join.
registration.loadError: Who can join could not load.
registration.onlyMeHint: Nobody else can join. People and invitations stay hidden.
registration.onlyMeUnavailable: Available again once you are the only person here. Delete the other people first.
registration.invitationOnlyHint: People join with a link you create. Each link works once and expires after 7 days.

saved.onlyMe: Only you can use this Calendar Ghost now.
saved.invitationOnly: People can now join with an invitation link.

links.copyUnavailable: Select the link and copy it.

step.title: Finish connecting your {account}
step.body: {provider} sends your browser to {origin} after you approve access. If that page did not load, copy its whole address from the address bar and paste it here. It works once, for 10 minutes.

note.body: If its page does not load after you approve access, copy the whole address from the address bar and paste it here within 10 minutes to finish connecting.
note.fix: To stop this, set the redirect URI for {provider} in .env to an HTTPS address of this installation, for example with Tailscale Serve, and register it with {provider}. Opening Calendar Ghost at {origin}, for example through an SSH tunnel, also works.

form.label: Address {provider} returned to
form.invalid: That is not the address {provider} returned to. Copy the whole address, starting with {start}

connected.title: {account} connected
connected.body: Calendar permissions were confirmed and the account is ready for Directional Sync Rules.

resumed.one: Access is restored. {count} rule restarted and catches up on changes made while it was stopped.
resumed.other: Access is restored. {count} rules restarted and catch up on changes made while they were stopped.

calendarPermissionRequired.title: Calendar access wasn’t granted
calendarPermissionRequired.body: No account was connected. Calendar-list and event permissions are required to discover calendars and run Directional Sync Rules.

authorizationFailed.title: {provider} authorization could not be completed
authorizationFailed.body: The account was not connected. Try again, then use Check access to confirm permissions.

connect.title: Connect a calendar account
connect.body: Authorize calendar discovery and event access for one account.

choose.title: Choose calendars
choose.body: Create a Directional Sync Rule with one source and one destination.

preview.title: Preview before syncing
preview.body: Review what will be written before anything reaches the destination.

connectionGuide.ready: Use a Connect button above to begin.
connectionGuide.notConfigured: Add the master key and a calendar provider's OAuth credentials in .env, then restart before connecting.

accounts.title: Connected accounts
accounts.intro: The calendar accounts whose calendars your rules can read and write.
accounts.notConfiguredNote: Add the master key and a calendar provider's OAuth credentials in .env, then restart before connecting an account.
accounts.loadError: Connected accounts could not be loaded. Reload the page and try again.

empty.title: No calendar accounts connected
empty.body: Connect an account to choose its calendars for your rules.

stopped.one: {count} rule stopped until it is reauthorized
stopped.other: {count} rules stopped until it is reauthorized

actions.disconnectHint: Removes its stored credentials. Rules that use it stop until it is reauthorized.
actions.reauthorizeUnavailable: Add the master key and this provider's OAuth credentials in .env, then restart.

resumed.one: {count} rule that stopped when access lapsed restarted.
resumed.other: {count} rules that stopped when access lapsed restarted.

body.one: Calendar-list and event permissions are available. {count} calendar is visible and {writable} can be used as a destination.
body.other: Calendar-list and event permissions are available. {count} calendars are visible and {writable} can be used as a destination.

bodySourceOnly.one: Calendar-list and event permissions are available. {count} calendar is visible and {writable} can be used as a destination. This account can still be used as a source.
bodySourceOnly.other: Calendar-list and event permissions are available. {count} calendars are visible and {writable} can be used as a destination. This account can still be used as a source.

disconnect.title: Disconnect {name}?

bodyWithRules.one: Its stored credentials will be removed. {count} affected rule will require reauthorization before it can run.
bodyWithRules.other: Its stored credentials will be removed. {count} affected rules will require reauthorization before they can run.

disconnect.bodyWithoutRules: Its stored credentials will be removed. No Directional Sync Rules currently use this account.

delete.title: Delete {name} permanently?

bodyWithRules.one: This cannot be undone. The account record and {count} affected Directional Sync Rule, including their mappings, cursors, incidents, and audit activity, will be removed. Existing Managed Projections in their calendars will not be deleted and will no longer be managed.
bodyWithRules.other: This cannot be undone. The account record and {count} affected Directional Sync Rules, including their mappings, cursors, incidents, and audit activity, will be removed. Existing Managed Projections in their calendars will not be deleted and will no longer be managed.

delete.bodyWithoutRules: This cannot be undone. The account record will be removed. No Directional Sync Rules currently use this account.

deletedWithRules.one: {name} and {count} affected Directional Sync Rule were permanently deleted.
deletedWithRules.other: {name} and {count} affected Directional Sync Rules were permanently deleted.

storage.title: Storage
storage.intro: Activity history and log files kept on this installation.

summary.emptyReclaimable: {size} · No Activity yet · {reclaimable} can be reclaimed

entriesReclaimable.one: {size} · {count} Activity entry since {day} · {reclaimable} can be reclaimed
entriesReclaimable.other: {size} · {count} Activity entries since {day} · {reclaimable} can be reclaimed

clear.counting: Counting the entries that would be removed…

body.one: {count} Activity entry older than {days} days will be removed. Each event's latest entry is kept. This cannot be undone.
body.other: {count} Activity entries older than {days} days will be removed. Each event's latest entry is kept. This cannot be undone.

nothingOldReclaimable.one: Nothing is older than {count} day. {size} left by earlier clearing can still be reclaimed.
nothingOldReclaimable.other: Nothing is older than {count} days. {size} left by earlier clearing can still be reclaimed.

clear.countFailed: The entries to remove could not be counted: {reason}
clear.reclaimed: The space left by earlier clearing was reclaimed.
clear.nothingCleared: Nothing was old enough to clear.

logs.title: Logs
logs.off: File logging is off. Recent lines are still in the container logs, which rotate.

help.body: Log files are kept unless CALENDAR_SYNC_LOG_DIR is set to an empty value. Set it to a writable directory, such as /data/logs on the data volume, or remove it from .env, then restart the service.
help.unusable: If it already names a directory, that directory could not be used: docker compose logs app shows the warning that says why.

logs.purgeBody: Every log line kept on this installation is deleted. Download them first if you may need them. This cannot be undone.

integrations.title: Integrations
integrations.intro: Optional. Tokens let monitors, dashboards, and AI assistants read whether synchronization is healthy. They cannot change anything.
integrations.summaryDetail: For monitors, dashboards, and AI assistants

issue.label: Issue a token
issue.hint: Name the tool that will use it.
issue.installationHint: Incidents about the whole installation and how many people are in each status. It names no rule, calendar, or person.

scopes.installation: Reads your synchronization status and Installation Health

reveal.title: Copy the token for {name} now
reveal.body: It is shown only once. Store it in your password manager or the tool that uses it.
reveal.copyUnavailable: Select the token and copy it.

revoke.title: Revoke {name}?
revoke.body: Anything that uses this token loses access right away. This cannot be undone.

status.issued: Token for {name} issued. Copy it now; it is shown only once.
status.revoked: {name} was revoked. Anything that used it has lost access.

transport.body: A token sent to this address crosses the internet unencrypted. Serve Calendar Ghost over HTTPS, for example with Tailscale Serve or a reverse proxy, before you use tokens from outside your home network.

examples.summary: Examples for monitors and AI assistants
examples.intro: Replace the token placeholder in each example with the token you copied.

installationHealth.title: Installation Health
installationHealth.description: Use a token that also reads Installation Health: incidents about the whole installation and how many people are in each status.

uptimeKuma.description: Add an HTTP(s) - Json Query monitor. Alert when the result is not false.

homepage.title: Homepage
homepage.description: Add a customapi widget to the Calendar Ghost service.

claudeCode.title: Claude Code

codex.description: Add this to ~/.codex/config.toml and set CALENDAR_GHOST_TOKEN.

desktop.title: Claude Desktop and other apps
desktop.description: Apps that start MCP servers on your computer connect through the mcp-remote bridge, which needs Node.js. In Claude Desktop, add this to the configuration file opened from Settings, Developer, Edit Config, then restart it.

theme.title: Theme
theme.body: Follow this device, or keep the interface light or dark.

darkPalette.title: Dark palette
darkPalette.body: The colors used whenever the interface is dark.
